Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Vantorre CX-10 refurbished combi

We paid $14,800 inc GST for this refurbished CX-10, delivered and commissioned on 14 September with a six-month parts and labour warranty. The listing said the steam generator had been descaled and pressure tested, and the core probe calibrated.

On 22 September, Kelsall attended for intermittent E34 low-water-level lockouts in steam and combi modes. The service report recorded nine E34 errors since delivery and an inlet pressure of 320 kPa, which the technician reported as OK. He replaced the water level sensor under warranty and tested three steam cycles successfully.

E34 returned four times the following week. We also found the core probe reading 63°C in a lamb shoulder when our Thermapen read 70°C. We repeated the check with the same result. On 6 October, the technician found the steam generator heavily scaled, descaled and flushed it, and recalibrated the probe to within one degree.

At 6.10pm on Saturday 24 October, E34 locked us out during a fully booked 60-cover service. We finished the lamb on the stove and in the deck oven, took pork belly off the menu and absorbed the cost.

Kelsall found further scale on 27 October and says it is a site water issue. They have advised that the attendance is not covered by warranty and will cost $280 plus GST, or $308. That is hard to accept for a unit delivered only six weeks earlier.

I checked with our water supplier after the October service: Fitzroy’s average hardness is about 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which they described as soft. The oven had been on our water for around three weeks when the heavy scale was found. That does not establish when the scale formed, but we would like Kelsall to explain how it attributes it to our supply, given the listing’s description of the refurbishment.

The technician has been professional, but the recurring fault and the disputed callout are worth knowing about before another kitchen spends this much.
